title: Web app manifest (app.yaml)
description: The manifest of a web app: the file `app.yaml` at the root of a deployment archive (docs/DESIGN.md, sections 9.1 to 9.10; decisions 20 to 26). Each live deployment is a version of the `webapp` node (encoding `app_release_v1`); the manifest travels in the archive, not in the node. The settings that are not in the archive (who may use the app, the telemetry mode, the report widget) are `AppSettings` of openapi.yaml. Binding targets are paths relative to the app node (`../garden.db`) or absolute in the tenant (`/Photos/Garden`) and are resolved to node IDs at deploy time. Step 3 accepts the runtimes `static` and `node22`; `python3.13` comes later in step 3 (decision 20) and fails validation until its card lands; `container` is not accepted in step 3. DRAFT for review (step 3 specify phase, docs/STEP3.md).

manifest_version.description: The version of this schema. Missing means 1.

runtime.description: `static`: files served from object storage through the gateway and the CDN (no process). `node22`: an OCI image built from the archive by the platform's builder (Railpack behind a `Builder` trait, decision 0006), run in gVisor with scale to zero. The build runs in the app sandbox with no secrets and no bindings. `python3.13`: later in step 3.

start.description: The command that starts the server (`node server.js`). Required for every runtime except `static`. It must listen on `$PORT` (the platform sets it).

build.description: The build command that the builder runs before the image is made (`npm run build`). Optional; without it the builder uses its default. The build is untrusted code: it runs in the app sandbox, with no secrets, no bindings, egress only through the proxy, and limits on CPU, memory, time and disk (decision 0006). A build from a repo node (step 4) runs it too.

static.description: The static part: the folder in the archive that the gateway serves, and how. For `runtime: static` it is the whole app; for a server runtime, the gateway serves these files and sends every other path to the server.

root.description: The folder in the archive (`dist`). Default: the archive root.

spa_fallback.description: Answer unknown paths with this file (`index.html`), for single-page apps.

headers.description: Extra response headers per path glob. The gateway always sets its own security headers (CSP frame-ancestors, nosniff); these cannot weaken them.

health.description: The path the platform calls before a deployment takes traffic (server runtimes). Default `/`. A `2xx` or `3xx` within 30 s passes.

check.description: The post-deploy browser check (design 9.6 level 1): the routes the headless browser opens. Default: `/` and the first five links it finds there.

resources.description: Limits of one instance and of the scaling (design 9.5). The plan caps them (`AppPlanLimits`); a higher value fails validation.

min_instances.description: 0 (the default) scales to zero: the first request after idle takes about 1 to 3 s (decision 25).

env.description: Plain environment variables (not secrets). A name that is also in `secrets` fails validation. Values are visible to everyone who can view the app.

bindings.description: What the app may reach (design 9.1, 9.4, 9.10). Each binding gives the `app` principal a role on a node, or scopes of another app's API. The deployer must hold that role (or the right to grant those scopes); else the deployment fails at stage `bindings` (checked before the `202`). In step 3 `edit` is accepted only on a database; a file or folder binding is `view` (the runtime API has no write path yet, decision 0006). A preview binds a database to a masked branch of it, every other node at most with `view`, and an API only with the called API's `preview_scopes`. The runtime gives the app one environment variable per binding: `RUUM_BINDING_<NAME>` with how to reach it (database: a connection URL with a short-lived role, no password in the archive; file or folder: the node ID for the runtime API; API: the internal address).

migrations.description: The migrations per database binding (decision 19): a folder in the archive with files `NNNN_name.sql`. At deploy time the platform runs the ones not yet applied, in order, each in one transaction with a restore point first (`applyDatabaseMigration` rules); a failure stops the deployment and nothing changes. On a preview they run on the preview's branch. Each migration may carry a `-- ruum:classes` header with the classes of its new columns (design 8.5).

secrets.description: The secrets the app needs (design 9.9). Values are never in the archive; they are write-only in OpenBao and reach only the running app, as environment variables. Previews get generated secrets with preview values and no entered secret, unless a user with `manage` turned on `preview` for that secret (`setAppSecret`, stored state; the manifest cannot ask for it: decision 0006-5). A list of names means `entered` for each (the short form of design 9.1). The long form says how each value is made: `generate` (Ruum makes and rotates it; most secrets) or `entered` (a person with `manage` pastes it once). There is never a database password: databases come through bindings.

access.description: Only the first deployment's value is used, as the initial `AppSettings.access`; afterwards the setting decides (`updateAppSettings`), so a new archive can never make an app public by itself. `public` needs the platform admin's approval for the tenant (decision 22).

roles.description: App-defined roles (design 9.3). Stored and granted by the platform (`app_role:<app-node-id>/<role>`). Every role includes the right to use the app. At most one role has `default: true` (the role of everybody with `view` and no explicit role) and at most one has `grants_roles: true`. When a version removes a role, its grants stay inactive; a rollback makes them active again.

claims.description: The facts about the user that the app asks for in the user token (design 9.4), beyond the pairwise `sub`, `roles`, `node_roles` and `actor`. The tenant policy can refuse a claim (no email for public apps); a refused claim is left out of the token, never an error.

apis.description: The APIs this app offers to other apps (design 9.10). `internal`: only apps of the same tenant that bind to it, at `http://<binding>.<api>.ruum.internal`. `external`: through the app gateway, for signed-in users with app roles, agents (Ruum can publish the OpenAPI as MCP tools, later), partners with API keys, or the public. The spec file is in the archive; a later change that breaks a bound consumer is refused by the breaking-change check of design 11.2 (step 5); in step 3 the deploy shows a warning.

protocol.description: `http` (OpenAPI file) or `events` (AsyncAPI file, NATS JetStream subjects through the platform bus).

preview_scopes.description: The scopes that a preview of a calling app may use (a subset of `scopes`; review R4). A preview runs code that no person approved, so it gets only the scopes listed here; without `preview_scopes` a preview gets no scope of a binding to this API, and its stage `bindings` warns which scopes were left out. List only scopes that cannot change data (`orders.read`).

granted_by.description: An app role of this app whose holders may grant the scopes to other apps, besides people with `manage` on this app (design 9.10).

audience.description: `external` only: who may call it. Default `[users]`.

events.description: Topics of the platform bus (design 9.10). `publishes`: the topics this app writes (declared in an `events` API). `subscribes`: Ruum's own events for nodes in a binding's scope (`node.created` below a bound folder) and topics of bound apps, by binding name.

path.description: The path of this app that receives the events (POST, at least once, with retries and a dead-letter queue).

jobs.description: Scheduled jobs (decision 21): the scheduler calls the path on schedule (cron, UTC) through the internal gateway, with a user token whose `actor` is the app itself. At most one run of a job at a time; a run that is still going skips the next one; a suspended app runs no jobs. Previews run no jobs.

telemetry.description: Telemetry (design 9.6). The classes of fields are in `telemetry-privacy.yaml` (`contracts/manifests/telemetry-privacy.schema.json`) at the archive root, or at `privacy_file`. Source maps under `source_maps` are kept private and never served.

browser_script.description: Set to false to leave out the Ruum browser script (no frontend errors, no report widget). Default true.

egress.description: Internet access goes through the egress proxy, which logs and limits (decision 23). `allow` narrows it to these host names; without it every host is allowed within the limits.

node.description: A path relative to the app node (`../garden.db`) or absolute in the tenant (`/Photos/Garden`), or a node ID (`node:<uuid>`). Resolved at deploy time; the version records the ID.

role.description: The role the app principal gets on the node. `manage` is never given to an app; migrations run as the platform at deploy time.

on_behalf_of_user.description: The app reads the node for the signed-in user (token exchange, design 9.4): the effective right is the user's right intersected with the binding. Default false (the app's own right).

delegate.description: Calls carry the signed-in user as `on_behalf_of` (a delegation chain, design 9.10): the effective right is the user's right intersected with this app's binding and the called API's scopes. The chain length is capped at 3 hops.

overlap.description: How long the previous value stays readable after a rotation (`RUUM_SECRET_<NAME>_PREVIOUS`).

STRIPE_KEY.description: Stripe secret key of the shop account

member.description: Can add plants and see the plan

admin.description: Can change app settings and grant app roles
